observations: Repeated US carrier activity against Palau/Truk followed by Marcus/Wake cannot be treated as isolated raids.
Japanese communications/route analysis and base reports indicate a broad Central-Pacific preparation cycle, although exact target and D-Day remain unknown.
Marcus/Wake neutralization increases the posterior probability of Marianas/Bonins-related operations more than a renewed Marshall-only campaign.

threat_state.exact_primary_island: UNKNOWN; Saipan/Tinian/Guam family recognized as plausible

Yamamoto_response: Keep five-carrier force in Sulu reaction geometry; do not sortie merely to chase TG58.6.
Increase submarine/picket emphasis east and northeast of the Marianas and along likely US carrier approach corridors.
Accelerate dispersion, airfield repair redundancy, fuel/ammunition dispersal and fighter/recon readiness in Marianas.
Preserve carrier air cadre for a landing-triggered fleet battle rather than trade it against shaping raids.
interservice_effect: Army aviation requests for China continue, but Central-Pacific warning now places a harder ceiling on additional first-line fighter/recon transfers away from Marianas/home-defense preparation.
